item.title: How an old fridge gets a second life in east China's Jiangxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
How an old fridge gets a second life in east China's Jiangxi-Xinhua How an old fridge gets a second life in east China's Jiangxi Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-11-26 18:57:05 FENGCHENG, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The industrial park in Fengcheng, east China's Jiangxi Province is home to many recycling enterprises that dismantle used household appliances to recycle metals and plastics. These metals are then processed and transformed into circuit boards, metal components, and other materials, which are reassembled into new household appliances and other industrial products. So, what happens to an old fridge after more than 15 years of service? Join our reporter as we take a closer look at how this old appliance is dismantled, recycled and given a second life. item.title: World's longest underwater shield-built highway tunnel reaches milestone in east China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
This photo taken on Nov. 26, 2026 shows the construction site of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel in east China's Jiangsu Province. China's self-developed tunnel boring machine (TBM) "Jianghai," with a maximum excavation diameter of 16.64 meters, has completed the 7.46-km tunneling work in the water section of Yangtze River on Thursday and successfully landed in Taicang of Jiangsu Province, marking that the right line of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel has been drilled through the Yangtze River. Stretching approximately 39.07 kilometers in total, Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel, connecting Haimen of Nantong to the north and Taicang of Suzhou to the south, is designed as a six-lane, bidirectional highway with a design speed of 100 kilometers per hour. (Xinhua/Ji Chunpeng) NANJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The right-hand bore of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel, the world's longest underwater shield-built highway tunnel, crossed beneath the Yangtze River on Thursday, becoming the first of the tunnel's two bores to reach the south bank. The country's self-developed tunneling machine completed the 7.46-km under-river stretch. The tunnel boring machine, named Jianghai, has a maximum excavation diameter of 16.64 meters. It began digging from the north bank in April 2025 and entered the under-river section that September. The crossing took about 14 months, with the machine advancing an average of 20 meters a day, according to Meng Defeng, who oversees shield tunneling for China Railway 14th Bureau Group on the project. The tunnel is a key step in building a major trans-river road link under China's longest river, connecting Haimen in Nantong with Taicang in Suzhou, both in east China's Jiangsu Province. Stretching approximately 39.07 kilometers in total, the tunnel includes an 11.185-kilometer underwater section made up of two parallel bores. Once open, the tunnel will shorten journeys from Nantong to southern Jiangsu and Shanghai, improving road connections across the Yangtze River Delta. China issued a plan in July this year to comprehensively advance the high-quality development of integrated transport services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the Ministry of Transport announced. The plan aims to largely establish a modern integrated transport service system by 2030. Under the plan, China will improve connections among different modes of transport, make passenger transfers more convenient and enhance freight logistics services. It will also promote the integration of transport and tourism, improve services at transport hubs, and strengthen rural passenger transport, freight and delivery services. ■ An aerial drone photo taken on Nov. 26, 2026 shows the construction site of the Haitai Yangtze River Tunnel in east China's Jiangsu Province. item.title: China's high-standard opening up creates new opportunities for global cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
* Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up. * From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services. * Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules. BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- At Friendship Pass on the China-Vietnam border in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, an improved customs inspection system has cut the time needed to identify pests in imported fruit to 36 hours or less, down from three to five days. This port handled durian imports worth 17.61 billion yuan (about 2.62 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of 2026, up 27.9 percent year on year, with China and Vietnam now jointly developing a smart border port to further facilitate cross-border trade. These efforts reflect China's broader push to expand high-standard opening up and develop new competitive advantages, a theme explored in the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency. BROADENING THE SCOPE OF OPENING UP Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up. The country's trading partners are becoming increasingly diverse. In the first three quarters of the year, China's goods trade with Belt and Road partner countries rose 17.1 percent year on year, accounting for 51 percent of its total trade in goods. Expanding into emerging markets has helped mitigate risks arising from slowing demand and mounting trade barriers in some traditional markets, making China's foreign trade more resilient, said Zhang Yan, a researcher at a research center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, trade with Belt and Road partner countries surged 35.3 percent year on year in the first nine months, according to Li Kaiyi, head of Yinchuan Customs. To overcome the region's geographical constraints, local customs authorities have piloted a new customs supervision model for rail-sea intermodal transport, boosting logistics efficiency by more than 30 percent. Local customs authorities have also helped wine producers resolve difficulties in obtaining certificates for exports to the European Union, with the value of Ningxia's wine exports to Germany and Spain more than tripling in the first three quarters of 2026, Li said. The potential for cooperation extends beyond the wine industry. Speaking in Ningxia, New Zealand's ambassador to China pointed to opportunities for technical exchanges between the two countries in wine production, livestock farming and crop cultivation. China's opening up is also creating new opportunities for foreign investors. In Hainan Province in south China, the number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises rose 31.1 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, with new projects including a Siemens Energy gas turbine assembly base and service center, said Wang Fengli, deputy director of the Office of the Free Trade Port Working Committee of the Communist Party of China Hainan Provincial Committee. DEVELOPING NEW COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES China's advances in science and technology and the development of its digital economy are also creating new opportunities for international economic cooperation. From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services, Zhang said. The country's exports of knowledge-intensive services grew 11.7 percent year on year to 1.2 trillion yuan in the first three quarters of 2026, accounting for 53.7 percent of its total services exports. Opening-up policies are also helping develop new businesses in high-value-added services. In Hainan, for instance, bonded maintenance and expedited customs clearance can reduce aircraft maintenance costs for foreign airlines by around 10 percent to 15 percent, Wang said. Meanwhile, digital cultural products, including online literature, video games and online dramas, are another growing area in China's services exports, Zhang noted. In Hainan's Chengmai County, a public service platform helps game developers overcome barriers to international expansion, such as cross-border network latency, regulatory compliance and payment settlement. The platform has attracted 125 enterprises and has more than 40 million registered overseas users. Under the policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) on secure and orderly cross-border data flows, this platform provides dedicated data links, reducing the costs developers would otherwise incur in arranging such connections themselves. DEEPENING INSTITUTIONAL OPENING UP Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules. The Hainan FTP serves as a testing ground for such reforms. Following the launch of island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports increased from 21 percent to 74 percent, Wang said. At the regional level, the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol brings cooperation in the digital economy, green economy and supply chain connectivity into an institutional framework, moving regional cooperation beyond tariff reductions toward greater coordination of rules, Zhang said. Greater openness also requires stronger risk management capabilities, Zhang said, suggesting that pilot free trade zones and free trade ports conduct stress tests in areas like cross-border data flows, financial opening up and cross-border services trade. Looking ahead, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) sets out measures to further expand the areas and geographical scope of opening up in an orderly manner, promote innovation in trade, and attract and utilize more foreign investment. "Regardless of changes in the international landscape, China will continue to counter external uncertainties with the certainty of steadily expanding its voluntary opening up," Zhang said, adding that China's high-quality development will create new opportunities for countries around the world. ■

item.title: China to put Y-20B military transport aircraft on first static display at Zhuhai airshow
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China's Air Force will put its domestically developed Y-20B large military transport aircraft in a static display for the first time at the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China, showcasing the latest advances in the country's military aviation capabilities. The Air Force will present more than 60 pieces of equipment across 33 types at the exhibition, scheduled to take place in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province, from Dec. 7 to 13, the Air Force said on Thursday. The exhibition will feature aerial demonstrations and static displays, showcasing the Air Force's latest equipment and modernization achievements. In the flying displays, the J-35A and J-20A stealth fighters, J-16 multirole fighter, Y-20B, and YY-20A tanker plane will demonstrate their capabilities. The Air Force's Bayi (August 1) Aerobatic Team will also perform alongside two foreign aerobatic teams, the Russian Aerospace Forces' Russian Knights and the United Arab Emirates Air Force's Al Fursan. In addition to the Y-20B, the Air Force will display a new-generation early-warning radar system and other equipment on the ground for the first time. Visitors will get the chance to tour the Y-20B's cargo hold and take part in simulated flight experiences. The Air Force military band will also stage performances and tours at the exhibition. Interactive activities will be organized across recruitment, talent development, military education, air traffic control and equipment maintenance exhibition areas, including presentations, consultations, simulated operations and immersive experiences. The exhibition coincides with the 30th anniversary of Airshow China. Air force leaders and representatives from multiple countries will attend international exchanges on military flight training and a forum on unmanned intelligent systems hosted by the Chinese Air Force. Distinguished representatives of Air Force units and test pilots will also meet with visitors, the Air Force said. ■

item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. additional tariffs on China, other economies: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes the imposition of additional Section 301 tariffs by the United States on China and other economies, a Ministry of Commerce spokesperson said on Thursday. The Office of the United States Trade Representative recently announced the results of its Section 301 investigation into alleged "overcapacity," proposing to impose additional Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China. Spokesperson He Yadong said at a regular press briefing that the U.S. Section 301 investigation is a typical act of unilateralism that seriously disrupts the international economic order and violates World Trade Organization rules. He noted that a certain country is using the pretext of "overcapacity" to pursue protectionism, politicizing normal market competition and turning industrial development issues into political tools. Such practices do little to address its own structural imbalances, but will instead disrupt the stability and security of global industrial and supply chains, undermine industrial cooperation, push up global inflation, harm the interests of businesses and consumers, and pose long-term systemic risks to global economic growth, he added. The spokesperson urged the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving differences through dialogue and consultation. China will closely monitor the developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests, he added. Responding to another media query on the arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction reached by China and the United States in September, He noted that China believes its early implementation would help expand bilateral trade. "We noticed that the United States had exempted products covered by the arrangement from the scope of its proposed Section 301 measures targeting alleged overcapacity," the spokesperson said. "We hope the United States will expedite its internal procedures and work with China to bring the 30-billion-U.S. dollar reciprocal tariff reduction arrangement into effect at an early date," he added. ■

item.title: China unveils roadmap for next-generation communication networks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese authorities have released an implementation plan for the development of next-generation communication networks, aiming to build such networks featuring comprehensive coverage and leading performance by 2030. The plan targets advancing 6G network development at an appropriate time and basically completing the construction of a low-Earth-orbit satellite internet system by 2030. China also expects to promote the large-scale development of integrated networks like the Industrial Internet and the Internet of Vehicles, significantly improve smart development, and further strengthen the industrial ecosystem, according to the plan. It sets out measures to improve basic networks, space-based networks and international networks, as well as integrated networks, while making communication networks smarter, greener, and more secure and resilient. Regarding the industrial ecosystem, the plan calls for accelerating the development of standards for technologies such as 6G, satellite internet and ultra-high-speed optical communications, and the integration of computing resources and communication networks. It also seeks to advance deep-space, deep-Earth, deep-sea and far-sea technological exploration, while promoting the integration of brain-computer interfaces, embodied artificial intelligence and intelligent connected vehicles with next-generation communication networks. The plan encourages private enterprises to participate in network development in accordance with laws and regulations and explore more diverse ways to engage. Stronger support should be given to securing land, forest, grassland, sea and spectrum resources for network development, according to the plan. Next-generation communication networks will form an intelligent, integrated digital infrastructure supported by advanced mobile, fiber-optic and satellite technologies, providing fast, secure and green connectivity. The development of next-generation communication networks is one of six network infrastructure priorities for China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), alongside water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, urban underground pipeline networks and logistics networks. Investment in these six networks and relevant areas is estimated to exceed 7 trillion yuan (about 1.04 trillion U.S. dollars) this year, the National Development and Reform Commission revealed. ■

item.title: Global delegates discuss water governance at millennia-old living heritage site in southwest China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
CHENGDU, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The main forum of the Dujiangyan River Strategy Forum opened Thursday in the city of Dujiangyan, southwest China's Sichuan Province, drawing about 200 scholars, officials and other delegates from home and abroad, organizers said. Gathered in the city, known for the Dujiangyan irrigation system that was built around 256 BC and remains in use today as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the representatives exchanged river management plans, devised strategies for ensuring water security, and promoted mutual learning among global civilizations. A think tank report on Chinese wisdom in river governance as seen from Dujiangyan was also unveiled at the forum. The report noted that the Dujiangyan irrigation system is the only ancient water conservancy project in the world still in use and one of the earliest successful practices of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature. Its construction fully reflects the Chinese nation's spirit of unremitting self-improvement, fearlessness in the face of difficulties, and pioneering endeavor. It highlighted the wisdom embodied in the ancient project, such as adapting measures to local conditions, following natural trends, harmony between man and nature, and managing water for the benefit of the people. The report was co-authored by the Xinhua Institute, a national high-level think tank affiliated with Xinhua News Agency, and the publicity and education center of the Ministry of Water Resources. Hu Yun, vice governor of Sichuan, said in his address that the province invested 286.9 billion yuan (around 42.76 billion U.S. dollars) in water conservancy from 2021 to 2025, with the ecological protection and governance of rivers and lakes seeing historic improvement. The province will seize opportunities to fully promote the construction of water network pilot zones and backbone water network projects, and strive to contribute more to the practice of water conservancy quality development, Hu added. Huo Xiaoguang, vice president of Xinhua News Agency, said the agency will fully leverage its advantages to better tell the story of China's water management in the new era to the world, share China's experience in river governance, and promote exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations around the globe. Xinhua will also aim to turn Dujiangyan into a window for the world to understand China, thus contributing Chinese wisdom and solutions to global water governance, he noted. Liu Dongshun, vice minister of water resources, said that since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China in 2012, the country has greatly enhanced its capacity to prevent floods and droughts, further optimized its water resources allocation, and fundamentally improved the overall condition of its rivers and lakes. Philippe Gourbesville, president of the International Association for Hydro-Environment Engineering and Research, said the Chinese government has clear goals and firm determination, and stands as an excellent model of river management internationally. He added that China has efficiently implemented many solutions, like establishing a system of river chiefs to coordinate action and management, while effectively managing and utilizing important water conservancy infrastructure, giving full play to its role in agricultural irrigation and river transport. China's rich experience can serve as a source of insights for France and other European countries, Gourbesville noted. At the main forum, attendees also saw the release of an initiative calling for safeguarding water security, protecting river ecology, using technologies for river governance, channeling cooperation to pool wisdom for global governance, and fulfilling the promise to manage water for the benefit of the people. The forum featured a main forum, a sub-forum and supporting activities, including on-site inspection of the Dujiangyan irrigation system and exhibitions showcasing achievements and innovative practices in China's river governance. The event was co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency Sichuan Branch and the Sichuan Provincial Water Resources Department. After more than two thousand years of continuous protection and iterative development, the Dujiangyan irrigation district, the country's largest, has expanded to 11.945 million mu (roughly 796,333 hectares), stably guaranteeing water security for production and daily life for 32 million people. ■

item.title: China unveils 2026-2030 services trade development plan, vows further opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China will expand the opening up of its trade in services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), according to a sector plan released on Thursday. The plan, jointly issued by eight departments including the Ministry of Commerce, says China will refine the negative list management system for cross-border trade in services, expand market access in an orderly manner, and improve the standardization level of this sector. The plan also aims to ensure the efficient, convenient and secure cross-border flow of factors including data, personnel, capital and technology. In particular, China will develop service infrastructure for cross-border data flows, deepen international data cooperation, and foster a more digital-friendly environment for trade in services, to facilitate the cross-border flow of data. "China's opening up in the services sector provides vital certainty to global trade in services," said Yang Zhengwei, vice president of the Development Research Center of the State Council. This opening up is expected to drive the growth of services trade, and the plan sets corresponding targets. By 2030, China's trade in services should achieve a better balance between imports and exports, according to the plan. In the first three quarters of 2026, China's imports and exports of services reached 5,768.77 billion yuan (about 859.78 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.5 percent year on year, while the deficit in this sector came in at 1,225.97 billion yuan. To boost services exports, the plan encourages professional service providers in consulting, accounting, legal, intellectual property and other fields to enhance their international service capabilities. It will also launch dedicated initiatives to promote exports in producer services, tourism services and cultural industries. Meanwhile, China will expand imports of producer services such as R&D and design, resource recycling and environmental governance. It will also encourage imports of more high-quality consumer services, including healthcare, cultural performances and sporting events. In addition, outstanding foreign audiovisual programs and films will be introduced to Chinese audiences, the plan notes. Li Bin, deputy head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, said China's services imports reached more than 620 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, covering travel, intellectual property, transport and business services, making China the world's second-largest importer of services. ■
